# Cardinality of the Eventually-Constant Sequence Set

## Identifying $D_n$

The set $D_n$ consists of all sequences $\langle d_k\rangle$ of rational numbers that are **eventually constant after position $n$**: there exists some $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that $d_k = q$ for all $k \geq n$.

## Computing $|D_n|$

A sequence in $D_n$ is **uniquely** determined by the finite tuple:
$$\big(d_0,\, d_1,\, \dots,\, d_{n-1},\, q\big) \in \mathbb{Q}^{n} \times \mathbb{Q}$$

where $q = d_n = d_{n+1} = \cdots$ (uniquely determined since $q = d_n$).

This gives a bijection:
$$D_n \;\longleftrightarrow\; \mathbb{Q}^{n+1}$$

Therefore:
$$|D_n| = |\mathbb{Q}|^{n+1} = \aleph_0^{n+1} = \aleph_0$$

## Evaluating the Proposed Equality Chain

The claim states:
$$|D_n| \stackrel{?}{=} |\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}}| = \aleph_0^{\aleph_0} \stackrel{?}{=} \aleph_0$$

**This is FALSE.** The critical error is the last equality. We have:

- **Lower bound:** $\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} \geq 2^{\aleph_0}$ (since $\{0,1\} \subset \mathbb{Q}$, binary sequences embed into $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}}$).
- **Upper bound:** $\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} \leq (2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$.

Hence:
$$\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0} = \mathfrak{c} \neq \aleph_0$$

So the correct picture is:

| Set | Cardinality |
|-----|------------|
| $D_n$ (eventually constant) | $\aleph_0$ |
| $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (all sequences) | $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ |

The set $D_n$ is a **proper, countable subset** of the **uncountable** set $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}}$.

## Conclusion

$|D_n| = \aleph_0$, but the proposed equality chain fails because $\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} = \mathfrak{c} \neq \aleph_0$, so $|D_n| \neq |\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}}|$.

$$\boxed{\aleph_0}$$
